Green Environment Youth Korea: Cohort 25 New Member Recruitment

“A future where we end the climate crisis with our own hands!” Green Environment Youth Korea (GEYK) is a nonprofit youth organization responding to the global climate crisis and working toward a sustainable future.

Our seven teams pursue practical, youth-led climate action through policy proposals, public participation programs, newsletters, UN climate conference activities, urban farming, and biodiversity study.

We’re inviting cohort 25 members to help find ways to address the climate crisis and make change from young people’s perspectives.

Recruitment Schedule

  • Written applications: August 11–21, 2026.
  • Interview shortlist: August 23, via individual email.
  • Online interviews: August 24–28.
  • Final decisions: August 31.
  • New member orientation: September 5. Attendance is required to retain your place.

Teams Recruiting

  • COP Team: Study the UN climate talks, organize Korea Pavilion side events and programs before and after COP, and explore opportunities to attend.
  • Climate Emotions Team: Research climate anxiety and its mental, physical, and social effects.
  • EMU Newsletter Team: Translate international news and write a weekly climate newsletter.
  • Urban Farming Team: Tend a garden at Yongsan Family Park and practice sustainable eating.
  • Biodiversity Team: Organize a youth biodiversity forum and develop conservation ideas.

See the recruitment cards for more details on activities and the qualities each team is looking for.

What You Can Do as a GEYK Member

  • Connect with opportunities to join national and local government committees and to speak or participate in specialist meetings and forums.
  • Take part in global climate discussions and build international partnerships. Organize COP-related events and explore opportunities to attend COP or represent Korean youth. On-site participation depends on circumstances and selection requirements.
  • Build a record of work with an organization recognized for its activities and awards, and meet young people from different backgrounds. Study and collaborate with people who care about climate change, whatever they study or do for work.
  • Develop practical skills through projects you lead, including research, report writing, content production, event planning, and translation.

How to Apply

  1. Download and complete the GEYK Cohort 25 application form.
  2. Complete and submit the Google Form.

For recruitment questions, send us a message on Instagram (@geykkorea) or email geykkorea@gmail.com.

Anyone passionate about climate action is welcome!
